title: Random forest links minimum night temperature to rice fat and fatty acid composition
summary: An interpretable random forest on six years of multisite field data from nine provinces in southern China identified minimum nighttime temperature during grain filling as the main driver of rice fat. Fat increased with this temperature while the unsaturated fatty acid index generally declined; patterns were checked in 2024 field trials at 11 sites. Projections indicate higher fat but lower unsaturated index under warming, and the evidence is observational.
ai_technology: Interpretable random forest model of field observations
organization: China Meteorological Administration; Beijing Technology and Business University

evidence.tested: Patterns were checked in independent 2024 field trials at 11 sites.
evidence.unknown: The physiological mechanism is suggested but not tested; projections are model-based. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest ranked climate drivers of rice fat content from multi-year field data.
